plainLanguage: Austin uses the 2024 residential and energy codes with its own local changes, effective July 10, 2025. Most new homes sit in SF-3 zoning: 25 ft front, 5 ft side, 10 ft rear and 15 ft street-side setbacks, 35 ft height, 40% building coverage and 45% impervious cover. In central Austin the 'McMansion' rules cap house size at the larger of 40% of the lot or 2,300 sq ft and add a sloping 'tent' you can't build through. Since 2024 you may build up to three homes on most single-family lots, and lots as small as 1,800 sq ft can hold one home. Big trees matter: trees 19 in or wider need a permit to remove and large oaks and pecans (24 in+) are protected. If you are near a creek, Austin uses the larger 500-year floodplain and wants your floor 2 ft above flood level. Expect about $7,700 in water and wastewater impact fees plus permit fees. New homes must have air conditioning.
